metadata.title: Why Soaring Profit Margins Might Not Be So Sweet<!-- --> - Barron's

content.text:
Why Soaring Profit Margins Might Not Be So Sweet
The S&P 500 index just posted its fattest profit margins in a generation, and the market is paying up for them. The index’s blended net margin reached 15.7% in the second quarter of 2026, the highest that FactSet has recorded since 2009. Post-tax corporate profits now run about 12.4% of U.S. gross domestic product, well above the long-run average of 7.3%. Investors are underwriting these levels as the new normal.
